title: Technical Writer
description:
About Alta Ares


Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 90 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

Role & Mission

As Technical Writer, you will own the documentation of Alta Ares' product suite — producing the manuals, user guides, interface specifications, and operational references that enable military operators, system integrators, and institutional clients to deploy and use Alta Ares' platforms with confidence.

In defence, documentation is not a nice-to-have. A military operator in a contested environment cannot call the helpdesk. A procurement officer reviewing an acceptance package expects documentation that is precise, complete, and unambiguous. Your work is the last line of clarity between a complex, cutting-edge system and the person who has to operate it under pressure.

You will work closely with Engineering, Product, and the Pre & Post Sales team — translating deeply technical content into structured, accessible, operationally relevant documentation. This is a high-craft, high-ownership role in a company where the quality of your writing directly affects operational outcomes.

Product Documentation — User Guides & Operator Manuals

  • Own the full suite of end-user documentation for Alta Ares' product portfolio: operator manuals, quick-start guides, field reference cards, and system overviews

  • Write clear, structured, and operationally grounded documentation for military end-users — adapting tone, level of detail, and format to the audience (drone operator, system administrator, field commander)

  • Develop and maintain documentation for each product line: ISR module, C-UAS platform, MLOps stack, GCS interface, and ground equipment

  • Produce multilingual documentation in English and French — ensuring accuracy and consistency across both versions

  • Maintain a versioned documentation library aligned with each product release and firmware update

Interface & System Specifications

  • Document software interfaces, system architectures, and hardware integration specifications in collaboration with Engineering

  • Produce interface control documents (ICDs), system description documents (SDDs), and integration guides for system integrators and institutional clients

  • Translate engineering schematics, API references, and architecture diagrams into human-readable specifications accessible to non-specialist audiences

  • Maintain up-to-date configuration guides, parameter references, and software release notes for each product version

  • Support the Engineering team in documenting internal technical standards and development guidelines

Operational & Field Documentation

  • Develop field-ready documentation adapted to operational environments: laminated quick-reference cards, checklists, and compact field guides

  • Produce pre-flight checklists, maintenance procedures, and troubleshooting guides for UAV platforms and C-UAS systems

  • Create training materials and operational scenario guides for use during client onboarding, field demonstrations, and exercises

  • Ensure all field documentation meets the usability requirements of military audiences: clear hierarchy, unambiguous language, and actionable step-by-step instructions

Documentation Lifecycle & Quality Management

  • Own the documentation lifecycle end-to-end: planning, drafting, review, validation, versioning, and publication

  • Establish and enforce documentation standards across Alta Ares: style guide, terminology glossary, formatting conventions, and review processes

  • Coordinate review cycles with Engineering, Product, and Pre & Post Sales teams — ensuring technical accuracy before publication

  • Manage the documentation repository in Notion and ensure all documents are findable, versioned, and access-controlled appropriately

  • Track and incorporate feedback from field deployments, client reviews, and post-sales observations into documentation updates

Client-Facing Delivery Documentation

  • Produce documentation packages for client deliverables: acceptance test procedures, delivery dossiers, and contractual documentation requirements

  • Support the preparation of responses to RFP documentation requirements and compliance matrices

  • Contribute to the development of training packages for institutional clients and partner integrators

  • Ensure client-facing documentation meets applicable defence documentation standards and contractual specifications

Candidate Profile - Experience

  • 3–5 years of experience in technical writing — with a strong focus on product documentation, user manuals, or operational guides

  • Prior experience documenting hardware-software integrated systems — mandatory : you must be comfortable with complex, multi-component products

  • Background in defence, aerospace, robotics, deeptech, or dual-use is a strong plus — you understand the operational context in which your documentation will be used

  • Experience producing documentation for non-specialist end-users (operators, field technicians) as well as technical audiences (engineers, integrators)

  • Prior exposure to documentation lifecycle management and versioning in a product environment

title: Senior Jet Engine Design Engineer – Interceptor Drones
description:
About Alta Ares


Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 90 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

About the Role
We are building next-generation interceptor drones and are looking for a Senior Jet Engine Design Engineer to lead the development of small-scale jet propulsion systems (12–25 kg thrust class), from concept to flight-ready hardware. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role in a fast-moving startup environment where speed and iteration matter more than lengthy upfront studies.

Responsibilities:

  • Design and develop new small jet engines (12–25 kg thrust range) in-house, optimized for very low production cost

  • Own the aerodynamic design of turbine components, balancing performance, manufacturability, and cost

  • Design a large portion of the turbine for metal 3D printing (additive manufacturing), leveraging design-for-AM principles to reduce part count, weight, and cost

  • Work closely with 3D printing operations to define printable geometries, tolerances, post-processing, and qualify parts for flight use

  • Drive a rapid, fail-fast iteration process: build, test, learn, and redesign quickly rather than relying on long analytical phases before prototyping

  • Integrate propulsion systems into airframes such as flying wings and other interceptor drone configurations, working with aerostructures and systems teams

  • Apply and enforce design rules for operation in extreme environments (cold and hot climates, rain, humidity, icing conditions) to ensure engine reliability across the full operational envelope

  • Contribute to engine testing (bench and flight), performance validation, and continuous design improvement

Candidate Profile:

  • Minimum 8 years of experience in jet engine / gas turbine design, with a proven track record of having designed and delivered engine models (not just component-level work)

  • Strong hands-on experience with small jet engines in the 12–25 kg thrust class

  • Solid global understanding of jet engine architecture: compressor, combustor, turbine, fuel system, controls, and their interactions

  • Experience designing turbine/engine components for metal additive manufacturing (DfAM), and practical knowledge of metal 3D printing processes and constraints

  • Comfortable working in a rapid-iteration, fail-fast development culture rather than a traditional long-cycle aerospace process

  • Experience integrating propulsion systems into airframes (flying wing or similar unconventional platforms is a strong plus)

  • Knowledge of design requirements for extreme operating environments (temperature extremes, precipitation, icing)

  • Ability to work autonomously in a small, fast-paced startup team, wearing multiple hats when needed

Nice to Have

  • Experience with UAV/drone propulsion specifically (vs. manned aviation)

  • Familiarity with low-cost manufacturing strategies for defense/dual-use hardware

  • Prior startup or skunkworks experience

title: Account Manager – Retention Specialist
description:
Notre mission ⚖️

Chez Doctrine, nous construisons le leader de l’IA juridique en Europe.

Notre conviction ? Le droit ne doit pas être ralenti par des tâches répétitives. Il doit être augmenté par une IA spécialisée, conçue pour comprendre, analyser et produire du raisonnement juridique avec un haut niveau d’exigence.

Notre ambition ? Permettre aux professionnels du droit de gagner en fiabilité, en efficacité et en sérénité, grâce à une plateforme unique, exhaustive et sécurisée.

Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance.

Notre développement est guidé par une approche claire : une vision globale, ancrée dans une compréhension fine des spécificités locales.

Derrière cette ambition, une équipe d’environ 250 personnes, réunies autour d’un même objectif : accompagner les juristes et avocats à toutes les étapes de leur travail, de l’analyse à la rédaction.

Et nous n’en sommes qu’au début.


Le contexte

Les cabinets d’avocats indépendants représentent le segment qui connaît la plus forte croissance chez Doctrine, avec une hausse de 50 % sur les 12 derniers mois.

Pour accompagner cette dynamique, tu joueras un rôle clé dans la fidélisation de nos clients et le développement de ton portefeuille. 

Nous recherchons un·e Account Manager (Retention Specialist) pour rejoindre notre équipe dédiée aux avocats indépendants.

Tu seras responsable d’un portefeuille de plus de 800 clients, avec une priorité : leur donner envie de rester chez Doctrine. Cela passe par des échanges réguliers, des démonstrations utiles à leur pratique et des négociations pour renouveler leur abonnement.

Tu travailleras avec les Sales Specialists, qui prennent en charge les ventes de produits complémentaires à partir des besoins que tu identifies chez tes clients.

Ce poste associe relation client, expertise produit et négociation commerciale, avec un impact direct sur la rétention et la croissance des revenus.


Les missions :
  • Contacter les clients qui utilisent peu nos solutions ou rencontrent des difficultés, pour comprendre ce qui bloque et les aider à reprendre leur utilisation.

  • Traiter les demandes de résiliation: comprendre les raisons du départ, répondre aux objections, démontrer la réelles valeur de doctrine  et définir une nouvelle proposition contractuelle pour ré-engager le client.

  • Anticiper les renouvellements d’abonnement et assurer le suivi des engagements pris avec les clients.

  • Réaliser des démonstrations et former les clients à nos solutions.

  • Identifier les opportunités business cross-sell et les transmettre aux Sales Specialists..

  • Organiser le suivi de ton portefeuille dans le CRM et suivre tes résultats : revenu conservé, renouvellements et clients réactivés.

  • Remonter les retours clients aux équipes Produit et Support, et partager avec l’équipe les approches qui fonctionnent.


    • À propos de toi :

  • Tu as une première expérience en vente ou en gestion de comptes B2B, avec des objectifs commerciaux.

  • Tu aimes convaincre et négocier. Tu sais écouter une insatisfaction, répondre aux objections et chercher un accord.

  • Tu es à l’aise au téléphone et prends volontiers l’initiative d’appeler tes clients.

  • Tu sais gérer un portefeuille conséquent, choisir tes priorités et tenir tes engagements.

  • Tu es curieux·se, tu apprends rapidement et tu sais expliquer simplement le fonctionnement d’un produit.

  • Tu apprécies les retours pour progresser et tu partages tes conseils avec tes collègues.

  • Tu t’exprimes clairement à l’oral comme à l’écrit, en français. Une formation ou une expérience juridique est un plus, mais n’est pas un prérequis.


    • Pourquoi être AM/Growth Retention chez Doctrine ?

  • Occuper un poste qui associe négociation commerciale, relation client et expertise produit, auprès d’avocats indépendants.

  • Être responsable d’un portefeuille de clients significatif avec pour objectif de les fidéliser et de développer ce portefeuille. NRR

  • Vendre et accompagner l’utilisation de solutions d’IA juridique qui évoluent régulièrement.

  • Bénéficier d’un onboarding complet, de formations et d’un accompagnement régulier pour progresser.

  • S’appuyer sur les équipes Ops et Marketing dans ton travail quotidien.

  • Bénéficier d’un package attractif avec un variable déplafonné.

  • Rejoindre une équipe qui se retrouve aussi lors de conférences, déjeuners, team-buildings et offsites.

    • Ce qui t'attend si tu rejoins Doctrine 🤝

    • Contribuer à un projet ambitieux, avec un impact réel et positif sur la société : rendre le droit plus accessible et plus ouvert.
    • Un onboarding très complet permettant une intégration et une montée en compétence rapides.
    • Une aventure dans laquelle la formation et le partage des connaissances font partis du quotidien.
    • Rejoindre une entreprise avec une vie d’équipe riche et dynamique : conférences, team-buildings, déjeuner, offsite, afterwork, etc.

    Nos valeurs 🤝

    Chez Doctrine, nos 4 valeurs nous accompagnent au quotidien et dans notre ambition de faire bouger les choses.

    • Challenge the status quo : nous défendons les idées audacieuses qui contribuent à l’évolution de tout un secteur.
    • Liberty and responsibility : nous encourageons l’autonomie, l’impact de chacun·e et l’ownership.
    • Knowledge is power : l'information est au cœur de la mission de Doctrine, et nous cherchons constamment à progresser.
    • Release early, release often and listen to your customers : nous croyons au pouvoir de l’itération et à l’importance d’écouter en permanence notre marché, nos client·e·s et leurs problématiques.
     

    Nos avantages pour faire la différence ☀️

    🏡 Une politique de télétravail flexible permettant - selon les équipes - jusqu’à trois jours de télétravail par semaine.

    👩‍⚕️ Une assurance santé avec Alan

    🍱 🚲 Une carte Swile pour tes tickets restaurants et ton forfait mobilité durable (66,60 euros par mois)

    💡 Des réductions et avantages négociés grâce à notre CSE via la plateforme Happypal

    🍏 Un équipement de travail neuf chez Apple

     

    Notre processus de recrutement 🚀

    • Un premier échange de 30 min avec l’un.e de nos Talent Acquisition Manager pour bien comprendre ton projet professionnel et te présenter ce qu'on construit chez Doctrine
    • Une rencontre d’1h avec ton/ta futur.e manager, pour détailler le poste et le scope de l’équipe, mais aussi répondre à toutes tes questions.
    • Un ou deux tests techniques pour évaluer concrètement tes compétences
    • Une venue dans nos bureaux pour : un déjeuner avec 3 personnes de différents départements chez Doctrine, pour te donner un aperçu de tes futur.e.s collègues ; un échange sur les valeurs de l’entreprise pour te partager notre vision, et une rencontre avec notre CEO, Guillaume.

Si cela peut vous rassurer, sachez que cette fiche de poste est indicative donc prenez la comme telle : c'est un guide, ni plus ni moins.

title: Product Manager  H/F
Head of FDE Learning Programs
description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

About the job

Mistral is hiring a Head of FDE Learning Programs to build the learning system for one of the company’s fastest-growing organizations. Mistral is scaling its FDE organization from its first hire to several hundred Deployment Strategists and Applied AI Engineers within two years. Your mandate is to make capability grow as fast as headcount without lowering the bar for customer work.

You will own:

  • Learning content: Build practical learning across three areas: technical skills, strategic and business capabilities, and product enablement.

  • Onboarding: Build a clear path from a new hire’s first week to independent customer work.

  • Technical bootcamps: Turn new products, research, and field methods into practical training for customer work.

  • Strategic bootcamps: Empower client-facing teams of FDEs to drive business and strategic discussions and to set up for success large partnership programs with customers

  • Program ownership: Own the roadmap, curriculum, contributor model, regional delivery, tools, measurement, and central team.

  • Scaling: Launch useful programs now, then adapt them for larger cohorts without making the content generic or relying on a small group of experts.

  • Team building: Launch the first programs, build a network of instructors, and hire the team needed to support several hundred FDEs.

  • Cross-functional work: Work with functional managers, Product, Engineering, Science, People, GTM Enablement, DevRel, and regional leaders.

  • Readiness standards: Ensure FDEs in every region meet the same standard, can find current material, learn from recent customer work, and understand expectations at the next career level.

  • Knowledge structuration: Ensure internal resources are up to date and pushed to the right stakeholders with a knowledge management approach.

How We Work in Solutions

  • We care about people and outputs.

  • What matters is what you ship, not the time you spend on it

  • Bureaucracy is where urgency goes to vanish. You talk to whoever you need to talk to. The best idea wins, whether it comes from a principal engineer or someone in their first week.

  • Always ask why. The best solutions come from deep understanding, not from copying what worked before

  • We say what we mean. Feedback is direct, timely, and given because we care.

  • No politics. Low ego, high standards.

  • We embrace an unstructured environment and find joy in it.

About you

You have helped build a learning, enablement, or capability function for a technical organization during rapid growth. You can start as the first dedicated owner, deliver useful programs immediately, and build the team and operating model needed to serve several hundred people.

  • You are technically fluent enough to work credibly with AI engineers, Product, and Science, inspect the substance of a program, and challenge material that is unclear or outdated.

  • You have designed programs that work across cohorts, regions, and experience levels without reducing the content to generic training.

  • You can lead work across senior stakeholders, subject-matter experts, managers, and operational partners without relying on reporting lines.

  • You can make firm trade-offs when hiring demand, expert capacity, and program quality compete for attention.

  • You pay attention to the full learner experience, including communications, scheduling, practice, feedback, and manager follow-through.

  • You use evidence to decide which programs to expand, revise, or stop.

  • You communicate clearly with executives, managers, technical experts, and learners.

  • You are fluent in English and can work with teams across regions and time zones.

Ideally, you have

  • Scaled a one-person or small learning function into a team and program that served hundreds of technical employees.

  • Built onboarding that kept pace with rapid hiring in an engineering, FDE, solutions, consulting, or professional-services organization.

  • Designed and operated technical bootcamps or other cohort-based learning programs.

  • Worked in technical DevRel, developer education, or a related role built around demos, code examples, workshops, and practitioner communities.

  • Built role- and level-based curricula connected to skills frameworks or career progression.

  • Managed a global program with contributors and learners across multiple regions.

  • Worked closely with Product, Engineering, Science, People, and customer-facing teams.

  • Designed practical assessments, readiness standards, or certification where appropriate.

  • Used learning platforms, knowledge systems, AI coaches, or program-operations tooling.

  • Worked in AI/ML or another technically complex and fast-changing field.

Why this role matters

Mistral is compressing years of organization growth into two. An FDE organization of several hundred people cannot depend on manager-by-manager onboarding, one-off sessions, and informal access to experts. If learning capacity trails hiring, ramp times would lengthen, standards would diverge, and teams would repeat the same mistakes across regions.

This role will build the programs, teaching network, and systems at the same pace as the organization. Two years from now, success would mean several hundred Deployment Strategists and Applied AI Engineers working from shared standards, learning new capabilities quickly, and improving the system with evidence from customer work.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

title: Engineering Team Lead, Sandbox
description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The team

Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. Our customers in finance, healthcare, and the public sector run frontier models on European-jurisdiction infrastructure, and the Cloud Platform team builds the systems that make that possible — compute orchestration, Kubernetes, bare metal, storage, networking, and the datacenter fleet that runs it all.

We run it all on our own metal, our own network, our own datacenters — which means when something breaks, the fix is ours to write.

European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on and shape the team building it.

The Role

This is a people-leadership role from day one. You will manage the team — hiring, coaching, performance, growth paths, honest feedback — while staying close to the code: roughly half your time in architecture decisions and the hardest technical problems the team faces, the other half leading your squad. If you are looking for a senior IC role, this is not it.

AI agents don't run in browsers. They run in sandboxes — and you will lead the team building ours.

We build secure, isolated, network-controlled environments with snapshotting primitives, designed for AI agents and reinforcement-learning workloads. An RL training run doesn't need one environment; it needs thousands, created and destroyed every second. An agent needs to be sandboxed from the world while still feeling fast enough to be useful. That tension — airtight isolation, at fleet scale, at low latency — is the product.

Your customers are the people building the next generation of AI software on our infrastructure; the primitives you ship become the runtime their agents live in.

What You Will Do

  • Build the isolation layer: microVMs or containers, namespaces, cgroups, seccomp, snapshot and restore.

  • Own the security boundary. Customers run code they didn't write and can't fully trust — your systems make that safe.

  • Scale to fleets: creation latency, density, and lifecycle management for thousands of concurrent environments.

  • Write Go alongside your team and own the architecture and the hardest implementation decisions.

  • Grow the engineers, not just the software — set the standard for ownership and coach people past their comfort zone.

  • Own people management for the team: hiring, performance, growth paths, and honest feedback.

  • Partner with Product Managers to turn frontier research needs into shippable primitives.

What We're Looking For

  • 2+ years of real people leadership. You have managed engineers — hired, coached, given honest feedback, and grown them. Hands-on contribution matters here, but this role is judged on the team you build and lead, not just the code you write.

  • Deep Linux internals: namespaces, cgroups, seccomp, virtualization — ideally microVMs of the Firecracker class.

  • You have shipped production systems in Go. Not dabbled. Shipped.

  • You understand network isolation at the packet level — not just firewall rules.

  • Performance instincts: you know what a syscall costs, and you have the profiles to prove you've cared.

  • 8+ years building backend or infrastructure systems.

  • You have partnered with product, design, and business teams to ship software that reached real users.

  • A low-ego, team-first mindset. We care less about your exact domain and more about whether you are the kind of technical force other engineers want to work alongside.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

This is a founding people-leadership role. There is no team to inherit and no legacy to maintain — you build the team as well as the stack, and you are accountable for both from day one. If you are looking for a senior IC role, this is not it.

You will be the founding Engineering Team Lead for storage on our cloud.

Block, filesystem, and object storage for training runs, sandboxed workloads, and general compute: you decide what we build, what we buy, and how it adds up to storage our customers can bet a business on. Some layers we deploy and harden from best-in-class vendors. The ones that matter most we write ourselves in Go — S3-compatible object storage, tiering, backup and recovery, caching layers that put cold data on cheap spinning disks.

As the team grows, the balance shifts toward people leadership, and you decide how fast. You will own capacity planning across datacenters and the architecture that keeps data durable when disks, networks, and entire sites fail. Storage is a strategic bet for this org: the team you build and the calls you make will define how a gigawatt of European compute stores its data.

What You Will Do

  • Stand up the storage stack — block, file, object — for training, sandbox, and general compute workloads.

  • Make the build-vs-buy calls: deploy and harden vendor platforms where they win; design and write our own services in Go where they don't.

  • Own the data plane: allocation, duplication, tiering, backup and recovery, S3-compatible APIs.

  • Plan capacity across datacenters and across failure domains — petabytes, not terabytes.

  • Build the team from zero: make the first hires, onboard and coach them, own performance and growth paths, and set the standard for ownership.

  • Partner with Product Managers to shape the storage roadmap and make the technical and business tradeoffs.

What We're Looking For

  • You have built storage systems — object, block, or distributed filesystems — not just operated them. You know what happens when a disk dies mid-write and when a rebalance collides with a backup window.

  • Deep distributed-systems fundamentals: durability, consistency, replication, erasure coding, failure domains.

  • You have shipped production systems in Go. Systems engineers coming from C++ or Rust who are ready to write Go daily should still talk to us.

  • You are comfortable with hardware reality: HDD, SSD, and NVMe tiers, and the economics of each.

  • 8+ years building backend or infrastructure systems.

  • You have partnered with product, design, and business teams to ship software that reached real users.

  • A low-ego, team-first mindset. We care less about your exact domain and more about whether you are the kind of technical force other engineers want to work alongside.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The team

Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. Our customers in finance, healthcare, and the public sector run frontier models on European-jurisdiction infrastructure, and the Cloud Platform team builds the systems that make that possible — compute orchestration, Kubernetes, bare metal, storage, networking, and the datacenter fleet that runs it all.

European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on and shape the team building it.

The Role

A datacenter is not a cloud until software makes it one. You will lead the team that turns arriving hardware into accepted clusters.

Cabling validation, burn-in, firmware, deployment validation, software stack install — all of it automated, none of it click-ops. Your KPI is time to acceptance: the hours between a rack being physically installed and it serving customer workloads. Across the industry that number is measured in weeks. You will drive it toward days, then hours, as we scale toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe.

This is a founding leadership role at the intersection of hardware and software. Early on it is deliberately hands-on: most of your time in the code and the architecture, some of it on datacenter floors, because the automation has to survive contact with the machines it runs on.

But the job is building and leading a team from day one — hiring your first engineers, coaching them, setting their growth paths, and running the rituals that keep quality high. As the team grows, the balance shifts toward people leadership, and you decide how fast. You shape this new team's charter and set the standard for how every future Mistral datacenter comes online.

What You Will Do

  • Build the delivery pipeline in Go: provisioning, configuration, validation, burn-in, network bring-up, software stack install.

  • Build the team from scratch: make the first hires, onboard and coach them, own their performance and growth paths — and set the tooling standards and the playbook every future site reuses.

  • Own time-to-acceptance and drive it down relentlessly — measure it, break it down, kill the slowest step first.

  • Work shoulder-to-shoulder with Hardware Design and Fleet Health — reliability starts at delivery.

  • Handle GPU fleets at scale: H100 and GB200-class nodes, InfiniBand and RoCE fabrics, and the failure modes they bring.

  • Partner with Product Managers and the datacenter org to plan delivery waves against capacity commitments.

What We're Looking For

  • You have automated bare-metal fleets — you have written the software that turns racks into clusters. If you have done it by hand, you resented it and scripted it.

  • Hardware fluency: servers, GPUs, NICs, switches, firmware — you can read a parts list and a topology diagram.

  • 8+ years building backend or infrastructure systems, with at least 2 years leading engineers — real people leadership: you have hired, coached, and grown engineers, not just set technical direction.

  • Deep Linux: you are comfortable well below the application layer.

  • You have shipped production systems in Go. Not dabbled. Shipped.

  • Willing to travel to datacenter sites when the work demands it.

  • A low-ego, team-first mindset. We care less about your exact domain and more about whether you are the kind of technical force other engineers want to work alongside.

title: Founding Data Engineer
description:
TL;DR Davis is hiring a Founding Data Engineer to build the data behind our foundation model, trained from scratch to generate buildings as geometric graphs. You will own the data end to end, from raw floorplans and synthetic generation to a canonical representation, curation, large-scale pretraining and the ablations that tell us which data actually moves the model. Here the dataset is part of the algorithm.

About Davis

Davis is an AI-native real estate company accelerating early-stage development and architectural design. Today developers coordinate four to five fragmented stakeholders over weeks or months. Soon they will need only one: Davis.

We turn every input that shapes a development decision into decision-ready outputs: investor-grade feasibility studies, investment analysis, and architect-certified designs, delivered in days. Every stage pairs our proprietary AI systems with expert review, so velocity never comes at the cost of reliability.

We closed a $5.5M pre-seed co-led by Heartcore Capital and Balderton Capital, with Yellow, Evantic and Entrepreneur First, alongside angels from the founding teams of Spacemaker, Black Forest Labs, Hugging Face, Supabase, Cleo and Spore Bio. We already work with leading developers and expect to support hundreds of projects over the coming year, deepening our research, our hiring, and our coverage of the development process end to end.

The Role

You will own the data our foundation model learns from, a model we train from scratch to generate buildings as geometric graphs. Part of the corpus comes from real floorplans as images and PDFs that have to become clean, standardized graphs. A large part will be synthetic, procedurally generated building graphs, geometry and rendered floorplans, with controlled variation in style, scan noise, annotations and furniture, each kept with its ground-truth graph automatically.

You will think about the whole loop, from raw and synthetic data to a canonical structured representation, curation and validation, the training dataset, large-scale pretraining, evaluation, data ablations, and back to improving the generator and the data mixture. You are senior enough to architect the data stack and set the data strategy, and hands-on enough to write the pipelines, run the experiments, train the models and do the ablations yourself.

What you will be working on

  • Corpus from raw sources. Turn real floorplans (images, PDFs, scans) into clean, standardized building graphs, with the geometry and semantics that make them trainable.

  • Synthetic data generation. Explore strategies to expand the dataset with synthetic data.

  • Canonical representation and curation. Define the standardized representation, then filter, deduplicate, quality-score and validate at scale, with versioning, provenance and lineage.

  • Pretraining data and mixtures. Assemble the training datasets, design the mixture and the curriculum, and blend synthetic and real data for large-scale pretraining.

  • Data ablations. Train models to learn which data actually helps, read the results, and feed them back into the generator and the mixture.

  • Evaluation. Build the eval harness (datasets, metrics, regression tests, monitoring) that tracks data and model quality over time.

What We Are Looking For

  • You have built the dataset, not just trained on it. You have personally built or generated the data used for a large pretraining run, from raw or synthetic sources, rather than only training on a dataset someone handed you.

  • Senior and deeply hands-on. At least 5 years of strong experience, senior enough to architect the data stack and set strategy, but still coding the pipelines, running the experiments and doing the ablations yourself.

  • Data as a first-class problem. A track record where the data itself is the object: curation, filtering, deduplication, quality scoring, mixtures, synthetic generation.

  • Strong engineering. Deep Python, clean and typed code, async and concurrency, distributed data pipelines, TDD culture.

Nice to have

  • Computer vision and document understanding, images to structured output, OCR, layout extraction, segmentation, geometry extraction, vectorization, raster to vector, image to scene graph, 3D or CAD.

  • Graph and structured scientific data, molecular, protein or scene graphs, meshes, CAD, BIM, 3D geometry, or relational and structured world data.

  • Synthetic worlds and simulation, a structured state to a simulator to a renderer to synthetic images with perfect labels, then a perception model, with an eye on the sim-to-real gap.

  • Foundation models from scratch, real involvement in a large pretraining run, not only fine-tuning.

  • Public evidence of data ownership, lead on a dataset, a Hugging Face release, a dataset card, a technical blog on your pipeline, or a talk on data curation or synthetic data.

  • GIS and geometry, parcels, zoning layers, projections, computational geometry or constrained optimization.

  • Multi-country data, heterogeneous sources, localization and varying rules.

Why Join Davis

  • Own the data end to end, from the generator to the pretraining mixture, as the person who defines what the model learns from.

  • Shape a foundation model from scratch, on a structured representation no one else is training on.

  • Work on genuinely hard problems, image to graph, synthetic worlds and large-scale pretraining, with your work reaching clients within days.

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity, at a founding level, in an early-stage company.

  • Join a world-class team, a mix of AI researchers, engineers and architects backed by world-class VCs.

More information about Davis, the team and the market we're going after:

Team

Mehdi (Co-founder & CEO) grew up in a family of architects and has lived this problem firsthand. He is a repeat founder who bootstrapped his first startup at 20, and graduated from Sciences Po and HEC Paris. Amine (Co-founder & CTO) is an AI researcher from École Polytechnique who worked extensively on discrete diffusion and turned down a PhD with Google DeepMind to build Davis. They started working together in July 2025 at Entrepreneur First's first European residency, a two-month lock-in in a German castle.

Today we are a team of twelve: technical profiles from Polytechnique, ENS and INRIA alongside architects and deep real estate expertise. We are small with an extremely high bar. If you want to work deeply on hard problems and see your work reach clients within days, you are the one we need.

Why We Will Win

Real estate is a $13 trillion industry that technology has largely bypassed. The professional services that feed it (design, engineering, feasibility, permitting) represent hundreds of billions in spend that no one has seriously automated.

Proptech spent the last decade selling SaaS on the edges of these workflows. It did not work, for two reasons: no professional wants another tool to learn, and no tool can automate work that runs on expert judgment. Davis makes a different bet. We do not sell tools, we sell the work, AI-generated, expert-validated, delivered in days instead of weeks. Every project compounds our data advantage across typologies, geographies and regulatory contexts.

Why No One Has Solved Architectural Design

Real estate development bleeds time and money in architectural design loops. Architects cycle through dozens of floorplan revisions to meet regulatory and client constraints, each round taking days, each missed constraint restarting the loop. Traditional CAD and BIM tools offer zero generative capability, and parametric tools only check constraints after generation, which leaves designs that frequently break under new zoning rules or irregular sites.

Generative AI has the potential to solve this, but does not yet. Fine-tuning image diffusion models on floorplans produces layouts that look plausible but fall apart under scrutiny: hallucinated rooms, mislabeled spaces, code violations no architect would accept. Pixel-space models have no concept of what a wall is or why a corridor needs to connect two things. Compliance-guidance techniques typically require segmentation at each noisy timestep, compounding errors and making major edits impractical. These layouts may look plausible yet break building codes, or need heavy post-processing before they are usable.

This is exactly the gap Davis closes. Because our model generates on structured representations rather than pixels, it produces compliant, editable plans from the start, and the data you build feeds that model directly.

We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV.

If you are drawn to what we are building but do not meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet all of the criteria. If that is you, please do not let it hold you back. We would love to receive your application.

Le poste

InsideBoard est la plateforme d'IA dédiée à la conduite du changement. Nous accompagnons l'adoption et la performance chez les plus grandes entreprises mondiales (Stellantis, General Motors, Michelin, La Poste, Pernod Ricard, et d'autres).
En tant que Solution Engineer, vous êtes le pont technique entre nos clients et la plateforme : vous participez aux ateliers client, vous captez les besoins, puis vous utilisez le développement assisté par IA (Claude Code, Windsurf et notre outillage d'agents interne) pour configurer, intégrer et étendre la plateforme InsideBoard, souvent dans la même semaine.

Ce n'est pas un poste d'ingénieur logiciel classique, et vous n'avez pas besoin de maîtriser toutes les technologies de notre stack. Vous orchestrez des agents IA sur un écosystème interne bien documenté (surface d'API, automatisation n8n, conventions pensées pour les agents).
L'IA écrit la majeure partie du code ; votre travail consiste à savoir ce qu'elle fait, à vérifier qu'elle fait la bonne chose, et à l'arrêter quand ce n'est pas le cas. Et vous portez la relation client sur le volet technique.

Vos missions

Face au client (environ 50 %)

  • Animer des ateliers de cadrage et de spécification avec des clients grands comptes (en français et en anglais), du kickoﬀ aux comités de pilotage (COPIL).
  • Transformer les réunions en livrables actionnables : spécifications fonctionnelles, matrices de statut, wireframes, guides d'intégration, guides utilisateur, comptes rendus avec décisions validées.
  • Défendre des arbitrages face au client : configuration standard ou développement spécifique, vision cible ou solution pragmatique, et assumer la recommandation.
  • Répondre aux revues de sécurité et aux questions de due diligence technique ; rédiger des analyses de cause racine en cas d'incident de production.

Configuration de la plateforme et données (environ 50 %)

  • Configurer la plateforme InsideBoard via son interface d'administration ou ses API : KPIs (formules, agrégation, fréquences), plans d'action et programmes de coaching, challenges, guidance, sections de profil, champs personnalisés, formulaires, notifications, imports d'utilisateurs, de départements et de tags.
  • Construire et maintenir des workflows d'automatisation n8n : webhooks, tâches planifiées, synthèses générées par IA, pipelines de contenu RAG, alerting d'erreurs centralisé vers Slack.
  • Scripter des opérations de données en Python ou TypeScript : migrations en masse avec discipline dry-run et rollback, audits de licences, rapports d'engagement, échanges Excel/CSV/SFTP avec les DSI clientes.
  • Brancher des fonctionnalités LLM pour les clients : synthèses de performance générées par IA, pipelines OCR, bases de connaissances RAG, conception de prompts d'agents.
Le profil recherché

Vous n'avez pas besoin de connaître toutes les technologies que nous utilisons. Il vous faut assez de profondeur technique pour superviser une IA qui les connaît : comprendre son plan, poser les bonnes questions, repérer quand elle dérive, et valider le résultat avant qu'il n'atteigne un client.

Indispensable

  • Une vraie maîtrise des agents de code IA (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf ou équivalent) : vous savez spécifier une tâche précisément, piloter l'agent, relire sa production avec un œil critique et vérifier le résultat. Vous savez aussi quand ne pas lui faire confiance.
  • Une capacité de contrôle technique : vous lisez un diﬀ ou un log suﬃsamment bien pour comprendre ce qui a changé et pourquoi, vous suivez un appel API de bout en bout, vous vérifiez la cohérence d'une transformation de données et vous testez ce que l'IA a construit avant de livrer.
  • Écrire du code de zéro n'est pas exigé.
  • Une aisance avec les API REST : authentification, pagination, rate limits ; à l'aise avec la plomberie de données JSON/CSV/XLSX.
  • Une excellente communication client en français et en anglais : vous savez animer un atelier, recadrer avec diplomatie et écrire des documents qu'un DSI lira.
  • De la rigueur et de la prudence avec les données de production : dry-runs, plans de rollback,logs. Vous faites mesurer deux fois à l'IA avant toute mise à jour en masse.
Un plus
  • Une expérience de développement (TypeScript, Python), utile mais non requise.
  • Une expérience avec n8n, Zapier, Make ou une plateforme d'automatisation similaire.
  • Une exposition aux écosystèmes d'entreprise : Salesforce, Dynamics 365, SAP , SSO.
  • Une expérience d'intégration LLM (API OpenAI/Anthropic/Mistral, RAG, conception de prompts).
  • Un passé en adoption SaaS, conduite du changement ou customer success engineering.

Ensuite, vous aurez un entretien d'une heure pour discuter de vos expériences, motivations et de notre entreprise avec  Sébastien
Vous rencontrerez votre future manager, Manan, pour discuter plus en détail du rôle, de vos compétences et de ce que nous pouvons vous offrir.
Enfin, un appel téléphonique avec Michael, l'un des directeurs d'InsideBoard AI, clôturera le processus.

description:

Pensés comme de véritables hubs d’innovation, nos cinq Centres de Formation et de Recherche  articulent leurs expertises autour de grands enjeux industriels, environnementaux, sociétaux et technologiques.

Leur mission ? Imaginer le monde de demain en alliant excellence académique et impact concret.

Vous rêvez d’une industrie propre, efficace et durable ? Le centre SPIN en fait sa priorité.

Énergie, environnement, procédés industriels… on y conçoit des systèmes pour produire mieux, avec moins.

L’objectif ? Limiter l’impact environnemental, réduire la consommation énergétique et booster l’efficacité.

🔧 Dans un monde en pleine mutation, nos équipes déploient leur créativité scientifique pour accompagner l’industrie du futur. 

Et vous, prêt·e à innover à nos côtés ?

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

En tant que chercheur postdoctoal, vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en recherche et innovation affecté au centre SPIN. Au sein de ce centre vous conjuguez curiosité scientifique avec un intérêt pour l’articulation entre problématiques de recherche fondamentale et problématiques indus-trielles.

Le centre SPIN est l’un des centres de recherche de Mines Saint-Etienne dédié à la recherche en génie des procédés et rassemble environ 80 personnes comprenant enseignants-chercheurs, postdocs, doctorants, stagiaires, et profite du soutien de personnels administratifs et techniques. L’activité du centre SPIN s’inscrit dans le périmètre du Laboratoire Georges Friedel (UMR 5307) et du Laboratoire Environnement Ville et Société (UMR 5600). Vous développerez votre activité de recherche au sein du département « Procédés de Manipulation de la Matière Granulaire » (PMMG) qui concentre divers expertises scientifiques sur les procédés de transformation et la caractérisa-tion de matériaux granulaires à partir d’approches expérimentales et numériques, ainsi qu’à travers différents champs disciplinaires allant de la géométrie mathématique à la chimie minérale en pas-sant par la physique des écoulements complexes. L’activité du centre SPIN, comme du départe-ment PMMG, est caractérisée par une forte interdisciplinarité ainsi que par de nombreuses collabo-rations avec d’autres institutions de recherche et d’enseignement en Europe et dans le monde, et profite de nombreux contrats avec des partenaires industriels.

La matière granulaire est un état de la matière particulier qui peine à être décrit par les lois de com-portement qui s’appliquent habituellement aux fluides, ou aux solides. Cependant une vaste majo-rité des matières premières transformées dans de nombreux secteurs industriels, ou des produits manufacturés, se présentent sous la forme de particules solides (grains de poudre, agglomérats, granulés, comprimés, etc..). La complexité de la dynamique de ces solides divisés émerge du grand nombre de particules solides concernées. En particulier dans le cas de particules solides transpor-tées dans une conduite de transport pneumatique, où l’écoulement d’un gaz le long d’une con-duite entraine les particules solides, les interactions avec les parois solides sont le siège de nom-breux procédés physico-chimiques. Au-delà des collisions élastiques qui entraînent le rebond de la majorité des particules solides sur les parois, des processus de fragmentation, d’arrachement de charges, d’échauffement local, etc. sont susceptibles de provoquer des transformations de la ma-tière transportée. Dans certains cas, la formation de dépôts sur les parois peut être observée et affecte négativement les performances du procédé de transport.

Le travail attendu sera de mettre en place un montage expérimental capable d’étudier les proces-sus responsables de la formation de ces enrochements à partir de mesures de pression, de débit, de charges électrostatiques, d’observation par microscopie, de caractérisation granulométrique etc. Différentes poudres modèles pourront être utilisées afin de reproduire les observations d’enrochement reportées dans la litérature. L’équipe d’encadrement sera constituée d’enseignants-chercheurs du centre SPIN ainsi que d’ingénieurs R&D de notre partenaire industriel ORANO.

ou d’un diplôme d’ingénieur

Nous accompagnons chacun de nos collaborateurs sur le chemin de l’excellence, avec la conviction qu’ensemble, nous pouvons avoir un impact durable et significatif sur notre monde.

title: PhD - Inverse modal identification of free-field radiated noise from unducted rotor-stator stages: from laboratory arrays to Open Fan flight tests
description:
Context:

This postdoctoral position is part of the European project TAKE-OFF (Clean Aviation programme), which is preparing the full-scale flight demonstration of Safran Aircraft Engines’ RISE Open Fan engine on the Airbus A380 flying testbed, with the aim of reducing fuel consumption by 30 % and entering service around 2035. Without a nacelle, the engine noise sources radiate directly into free field. LMFA (École Centrale de Lyon), in collaboration with LVA (INSA Lyon), is in charge of analysing the near-field pressure data acquired in flight by microphones installed on the fuselage, in order to reconstruct the engine noise sources.

Objective:

To extend the modal analysis methods developed at LMFA for ducted engines [1] to unducted fans. For the first time, modal analysis will be applied to microphones located in an unconfined medium and to modes radiating under free-field conditions, and design criteria specific to this configuration will be established (spatial sampling, resolution, array-to-rotor distance relative to the array size).

Description:

Task 1 – Model and inverse problem. Build a set of eigenfunctions describing the radiation of an unducted rotor-stator stage (spinning modes weighted by Bessel functions [2], spherical harmonics, etc.) and embed it in a Bayesian inverse approach [1] to estimate the modal amplitudes of tonal and broadband components. Flow and fuselage effects may be accounted for through CAA computations.

Task 2 – Validation on the MAMBO database. The developments will be tested on an unducted propeller + stator configuration recently studied at LMFA (MAMBO project), instrumented with three arrays: a half-cylindrical array, a planar array on the side (representative of fuselage instrumentation) and a motorised arc array measuring directivity, which will serve as an independent reference. This study will assess the robustness of the method and define array design criteria.

Task 3 – Application to flight tests. The methodology will be applied to the near-field pressure data acquired on the fuselage during the TAKE-OFF flight test campaigns, in order to identify the modal content of the noise radiated by the Open Fan engine and to infer information on its generation mechanisms.

Starting date : 01/01/2027


Profile and application:

PhD in acoustics, aeroacoustics or signal processing; skills in array methods, inverse problems and/or modal analysis; scientific programming (Python/Matlab).

References:

[1] Pereira, A. & Jacob, M.C., 2022, Modal analysis of in-duct fan broadband noise via an iterative Bayesian inverse approach, J. Sound Vib., doi:10.1016/j.jsv.2021.116633.

[2] Roger, M. & Kucukcoskun, K., 2019, Near-and-far field modeling of advanced tail-rotor noise using source-mode expansions, J. Sound Vib., 453, 328-354.

LMFA contacts: Antonio Pereira, Marc Jacob

LVA contact: Quentin Leclère (LVA, INSA Lyon)

Funding: European project TAKE-OFF (Technology and Knowledge for European Open Fan Flight)
